title: POC scoping - open models for NovaPack
next_steps: Maya to share benchmark spreadsheet and security pack by 2027-01-18
Run 3-model benchmark (Llama-3 8B, Mistral-instruct, MPT-7B) on NovaPack dataset week of 2027-01-25
Diego to provide Redwood Dedicated config options and preliminary cost estimates by 2027-01-20
Schedule follow-up demo to review benchmark results (30 min) week of 2027-02-01
action_items: Maya Patel: send pricing & security docs (SOC2/ISO) by 2027-01-18
Diego Ramos: prepare benchmark run configs and sample inference script by 2027-01-20
Anika Roy: share a 1-week sample of labeled customer support transcripts (anonymized) by 2027-01-19
summary: Discovery + POC scoping focused on selecting an open-model shortlist for NovaPack's multilingual customer support summarization workload. Primary success criteria: latency < 500ms token latency on 4k context, F1/ROUGE targets vs current baseline, cost per 1M tokens under target, and privacy requirements (no external retention). Agreed next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, run 3-model POC on anonymized week of transcripts, and reconvene to review results.
topics: Workload sizing (qps, token distribution, context lengths)
Benchmark plan & metrics (ROUGE, F1, latency p50/p95)
Model shortlist (Llama-3 8B, Mistral-instruct, MPT-7B / RedPajama variants)
Deployment options (hosted API vs Dedicated vs VPC)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, part of the team that runs POCs and infra for inference, Diego is our SE. Can you quickly intro?
[00:10] James: Hey all, James here, CTO at NovaPack, we've got Anika and Ethan with us. We want to scope a POC for summarization and routing across English, Spanish and French support tickets.
[00:22] Diego: Awesome. Before we dive, quick logistics — we'll propose a 3-model shortlist, run bench on a 1-week anonymized dataset, measure quality and latency, and then pick a winner for a short pilot.
[00:34] Anika: Sounds good; our baseline is a custom fine-tuned model hosted on prem, roughly 200 qps at peak, average ticket size ~1.1k tokens but with long tails up to 6k.
[00:45] Ethan: Our success metrics are: comparable or better summary quality than current (ROUGE-1/2, precision/recall), p95 latency under 1.2s for end-to-end, and cost delta under 30% vs current infra. Also strict data residency - no long-term storage in third party.
[01:05] Maya: Got it. On the storage/privacy front Redwood Private / VPC option supports customer-managed KMS and no retention by default — that aligns with your needs.
[01:18] James: Good. For timelines, we want initial results in two weeks and a pilot in 6 weeks if numbers look good. Is that doable?
[01:26] Diego: Two weeks for an initial run is tight but doable if you can share the anonymized sample by Tues. We'll run three models: Llama-3 8B (quantized), Mistral-instruct variant, and MPT-7B or RedPajama instruct — we'll pick versions optimized for summarization.
[01:40] Anika: Why those three? Any thoughts on multilingual quality?
[01:44] Diego: Tradeoffs: Llama-3 tends to be strong on instruction following and multilingual, Mistral has great English performance at a lower cost, MPT variants are lightweight and fast but sometimes weaker in non-English. RedPajama derivatives can be strong if you pick a model with multilingual fine-tuning. We'll detail expected quality tradeoffs in the bench sheet.
[02:05] Ethan: What about tokenization/context handling for long tickets? We have a lot of >4k contexts.
[02:12] Maya: We'll test two approaches: prefix summarization where we chunk and then aggregate, and extended context models (8k if available). Redwood runtime supports KV cache and efficient attention kernels — though sometimes transcripts say K V cash haha — but we will measure memory and latency.
[02:30] James: Latency budget per request is 1.2s p95, but we prefer p50 lower. How do you measure per-token latency vs end-to-end?
[02:39] Diego: We'll report both: model token-latency p50/p95 and end-to-end including network and aggregation. For dedicated pools we can meet tighter tail latency via reserved capacity.
[02:50] Anika: For benchmarks, our labeled metric is ROUGE-L F1 on human summaries. We can provide 500 holdout tickets with gold summaries.
[02:58] Maya: Perfect — send that and we'll wire it into the bench harness.
[03:03] Ethan: Cost expectations — what pricing assumptions should we use for open models?
[03:08] Diego: We'll provide per-model estimated inference cost based on tokens/sec and GPU-hour pricing. For quantized 8B variants cost drops significantly. Redwood Optimize will also suggest batching and KV cache settings to reduce unit cost.
[03:21] James: Any SOC2 / compliance paperwork available?
[03:24] Maya: Yes, we'll attach our SOC2 report and an architecture note for VPC/private deployments. You'll get those in the security pack.
[03:31] Anika: For multilingual, we also need domain-specific terminology handling, especially French pharma terms. Can the models be adapted quickly?
[03:40] Diego: Two options: short instruction-tuning via adapters or few-shot in-prompt examples, or light continued pretraining if you want persistent improvement. For POC we'll do prompt + in-context examples and a small adapter if needed. Note: adapter training time adds days.
[04:00] Maya: Just to surface potential gotchas — some open-model checkpoints differ by tokenizer which can affect token counts and cost. We'll normalize by working in the bench harness to ensure apples-to-apples.
[04:12] Ethan: Good point. Also can we test both hosted Redwood API and a Dedicated pool to compare costs?
[04:18] Diego: Yes — we'll run bench in three modes: hosted lowest friction, dedicated reserved pool (predictable tail), and a VPC/private config to simulate your compliance setup.
[04:29] James: On data flow: during test runs will any data leave our VPC? We need to ensure no retention and no external logging.
[04:36] Maya: For the private run, no. For hosted runs we'll disable retention and sign BAA if required; we'll document exact retention policies in the security doc.
[04:45] Anika: Bench metrics — can you include p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, cost per 1M tokens, ROUGE, and a qualitative error analysis bucketed by language?
[04:55] Diego: Absolutely. We'll add a column for domain failure modes — e.g., hallucinations on rare terminology.
[05:02] Ethan: Acceptable thresholds — company wants precision>0.82 on summary extractive measures and recall>0.78, these are rough.
[05:11] Maya: We'll use those targets as pass/fail for the POC. If the model doesn't meet thresholds but is cheaper, we'll flag tradeoffs in the writeup.
[05:19] James: How many tokens should we provision for bench runs?
[05:23] Diego: If you share a week sample, we can compute real token distribution, but we typically run 10k to 50k inference calls for stable metrics. For you, 20k calls covering long-tail contexts would be sound.
[05:33] Anika: We can anonymize and subset to 25k.
[05:36] Maya: Great. Timeline recap: Anika shares data by 2027-01-19, Diego sets up bench & infra by 2027-01-20, bench runs week of 2027-01-25, results + follow-up week of 2027-02-01.
[05:47] Ethan: Who will be the technical owner on Redwood side?
[05:50] Maya: Diego will own the bench configs and run; I'll be AE and handle security/pricing.
[05:55] James: Any red flags for long-term production?
[05:58] Diego: Watch model drift and quantization artifacts — we'll include quality monitoring hooks in Redwood Console and alerts if ROUGE drops on the eval set. Also caching can reduce cost but may increase stale context risks; we'll advise TTLs.
[06:14] Anika: For the POC can we do a small fine-tuning step if none of the models hit thresholds?
[06:18] Diego: Yes, but it adds time and infra. We'll show few-shot/adapter first. If needed, TAT for fine-tune ~1-2 weeks depending on data size.
[06:27] Maya: I'll put both options in the bench doc as contingency.
[06:30] Ethan: Any specific benchmark datasets you use as priors?
[06:33] Diego: We use an internal suite and will add your gold summaries; we'll compute ROUGE, BLEU and a human review sample for edge cases.
[06:43] James: Are there vendor lock considerations? For example, if we go with a model variant tied to a custom runtime?
[06:48] Maya: We try to avoid lock-in; Redwood's model catalog supports switching model variants and fallbacks. You can pin versions and we can snapshot inference configs.
[06:57] Anika: Regarding multilingual, is there an obvious winner among shortlisted models?
[07:01] Diego: Llama-3 8B is the most balanced for multi language, Mistral is cost-effective for English heavy, MPT can be tuned for low-latency but may need extra work for non-English. We'll validate on your French subset specifically.
[07:14] Ethan: Ok let's confirm the model list in doc: Llama-3 8B q4_k, Mistral-instruct v1, MPT-7B-instruct, and RedPajama-instruct as a wildcard.
[07:25] Maya: Yep we'll list those and note expected memory/latency.
[07:30] James: Anything else on infra sizing? Peak 200 qps, but average 60 qps — some burst.
[07:36] Diego: For Dedicated we recommend a reserved pool sized for 200 qps contended; autoscale to handle bursts. We'll give both GPU count and expected concurrency numbers.
[07:47] Anika: For evaluation, can we also test hallucination rate and factuality on ticket metadata?
[07:52] Diego: We'll include a hallucination metric bucket; often it's manual but we'll sample 200 outputs for human review.
[07:59] Maya: Quick note — sharing the security pack and bench spreadsheet after the call. Also Diego will share the bench harness repo link and a sample inference script.
[08:10] Ethan: Great. One more question — can Redwood run a private on-prem deployment for the pilot?
[08:15] Maya: Yes, we offer Private on-prem and VPC, but that adds setup time and an enterprise license. We'll show the timeline differences in the doc.
[08:25] James: Thanks. Let's recap next steps.
[08:28] Maya: Recap: Anika send data by 2027-01-19; Maya send security & pricing by 2027-01-18; Diego spin bench and provide configs by 2027-01-20; bench week of 01-25; review week of 02-01.
[08:40] Ethan: Thanks everyone.
[08:42] James: Thanks — talk soon.
[08:45] [call ends]

Note: transcription occasionally mislabels speakers and has minor ASR errors (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache). References shared: bench spreadsheet (link in follow-up), Redwood security pack (link), bench harness repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness (sample).
